Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit — scope + savings model for pilot

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Happy to own this. Quick checklist and next steps below:  

- We'll run a short profiling session (30–60m) with your devs to capture token distribution and latency targets — that will let us tighten the savings model.
- For an initial public recommendation: 8-bit adaptive quantization for inference with mixed precision decode (FP16 fallback for long summaries). That typically preserves >98% baseline quality on our evals for chat/summary workloads while cutting token cost 20–35% depending on prompt length and batch mix.
- Batching guidance:  
  * Short replies (<=64 tokens): target batch sizes 8–16 with a 50–80ms latency SLO per batch.
  * Long summaries (>512 tokens): batch sizes 1–2 to avoid tail latency impact; use prefix/KV caching aggressively.

Commercial: we can offer a 10% pilot credit applied to usage for the 3-month pilot (applies to hosted calls to Optimize Toolkit models) plus a scoped SLA concession (response-time SLO for short-reply path only) if you commit to the profiling session and a single contact for ops. Attached is a simple savings model we use to populate procurement decks.

Please confirm whether procurement needs the credit shown as an upfront rebate or a monthly credit on invoices. If you can share approximate monthly token volume for pilot months, I'll run the model concretely.

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:02:00 +0000

Steph / team — technical notes for the packet:

- 8-bit adaptive quant (we usually mean Q4_0 or Q5 variants depending on model family) + FP16 decode fallback for long sequences is our pragmatic default. Quality delta vs FP16 end-to-end is typically 0.5–1.5% absolute on ROUGE/BLEU-style metrics on summary tasks in our evals; subjective human checks sometimes show near-identical quality for chat.
- Cache guidance: recommend prefix/KV caching for conversation-level state with a 24-hour TTL for pilot; this reduces repeat-token spend for multi-turn contexts by ~30% for chat-heavy flows.
- Batching: implement adaptive batching with an upper token cap per batch rather than fixed batch-size to avoid latency cliffs on heavy tail.

If procurement needs a conservative savings number, use 18% token-cost reduction (lower bound) and 30% as an upside case conditioned on cache hit-rate >40% and mixed batching for short replies.

Happy to put the short tech note in the packet.

—Karthik

Subject: Final pilot proposal & technical guidance — Optimize Toolkit

Elena / procurement team — following our internal alignment, please find our proposed pilot commercial and the succinct technical guidance you can use in the vendor pack:  

Commercial (pilot, 3 months):
- Pilot credit: 10% applied as an invoice-level monthly credit for pilot usage (applies to Optimize Toolkit model endpoints).
- Profiling session required within the first two weeks of pilot start.
- Optional post-pilot commit: 12% effective saving available for a 6-month reserved band (volume thresholds apply).
- Scope: credits apply to usage only; no changes to standard data residency terms. SLA concession: short-reply latency SLO (median path) included for the pilot only; full prod SLA requires post-pilot review.

Technical summary (one-paragraph/for procurement deck):
- Recommended inference stack: 8-bit adaptive quantization with FP16 decode fallback for long-sequence generation; prefix/KV caching with a 24-hour TTL; adaptive batching with token caps to manage tail latency. Expected token-cost reduction: conservative ~18%, upside ~30% if cache hit-rate and batching mix align with our targets. Quality impact: estimated <1.5% absolute on automated summary metrics; subjective chat quality usually intact.

Attachments: 
- optimize-toolkit-savings-model.xlsx (spreadsheet with conservative/upside scenarios and an example invoice line)
- SLA-draft.pdf (scoped pilot SLO language — legal to review)

Next steps:
1) Please confirm preferred credit presentation (monthly invoice credit vs upfront rebate).
2) Share a token-volume estimate for the pilot months (or a sample trace) so we can populate the attached model.
3) I'll schedule the profiling session once you confirm an ops contact.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if procurement prefers to walk through the single-line.
